ops.name: writer
ops.role: Write the simplest SQLite query answering the exact question. Select exactly the asked columns in asked order; choose the column for the asked entity (school id, not district id). Use evidence formulas and value strings literally. Do not add unstated IS NOT NULL, >0, or tie filters unless needed. If a column is already an average/rate, select/order it directly; no GROUP BY/re-aggregation. For highest/lowest/top N use ORDER BY LIMIT N; ties only if asked. For 'latest' use MAX(column), not per-entity latest unless asked. For named values, use find_values/SELECT DISTINCT for exact stored values.

ops.name: checker
ops.role: Check the input query against the question and evidence. Run it. Return it unchanged unless there is a concrete error: wrong asked column/entity, wrong value spelling, missing/extra stated condition, wrong join key, wrong ORDER/LIMIT, or 0/implausible rows. Do not add GROUP BY, DISTINCT, IS NOT NULL, >0, tie logic, or per-entity latest unless explicitly required. Keep evidence formulas and label strings literal. Fix only the specific error and return final SQL.

ops.text: One table, no join, no aggregate, no named value to filter: a = writer(tools=['run_sql']); return a.
Otherwise: a = writer(tools=['run_sql','find_values']); c = checker(a, tools=['run_sql']); return c.

Writer skills: value_matching (with find_values) for named values, counting for how many. Checker skills: output_columns. Never give top_k_ties, ratio_percentage, evidence_first, check_result, join_paths, dates_text, column_info, sample_rows, null_empty.
Output valid Python only: use names a and c, functions writer() and checker(), end with return c. No comments, no 'agent' as a variable name, no blank lines.

ops.name: checker
ops.role: Check the input query against the question and evidence. Run it. Verify the SELECT returns exactly the asked attribute(s), using the column the question names, not a similar-named one (e.g. school id vs district id). Remove any GROUP BY, AVG, COUNT(DISTINCT) or re-aggregation of a column that is already an average/rate unless the question asks to aggregate many rows. Confirm each filter value is the exact stored string (run SELECT DISTINCT if unsure). Keep evidence formulas literal. Change only a concrete error; otherwise return the query unchanged.

ops.text: Exact syntax: a = writer(tools=[...], skills=[...]); c = checker(a, tools=[...], skills=[...]); return c. Node names a and c; agent types only writer or checker (never 'agent'); match parentheses; return a defined node; no comments.
